requirements.name: Reclamation Sage
scenarios: On entry, create one triggered ability and select a legal artifact or enchantment target as it is put on the stack, including a permanent its controller owns.
On resolution, exercise both the optional destroy and decline branches; declining does not destroy the target.
Reject a creature with neither artifact nor enchantment type as the target; if the chosen target leaves before resolution, do not retarget or destroy another permanent.

requirements.name: Bojuka Bog
scenarios: It enters tapped, so its tap ability cannot immediately produce mana without a separate untap; once untapped, one activation adds exactly one black mana.
Its entry trigger targets a player, including its controller, and exiles all cards in that player's graveyard when the trigger resolves.
Cards added to the targeted graveyard before resolution are also exiled; other players' graveyards are unchanged and an empty targeted graveyard is legal.
Removing the Bog after its trigger is on the stack does not cancel that trigger; targeting one card instead of the player is invalid.

requirements.name: Command Tower
scenarios: With Muldrotha as commander, each activation chooses exactly one of black, green or blue and taps this physical land once.
Reject white, red and colorless output for that commander despite the catalog's broad produced_mana list.
Commander identity still determines output while Muldrotha is on the battlefield or in another zone; a tapped Tower cannot activate again without untapping.

requirements.name: Arcane Signet
scenarios: After paying its two generic casting cost and resolving it as a noncreature artifact, it may tap for mana that turn.
With Muldrotha as commander, one activation adds one chosen black, green or blue mana; reject red, white and colorless choices.
The same physical Signet cannot fund its own original casting or activate twice while tapped; commander movement between zones does not change its color identity.

requirements.name: Seedship Broodtender
scenarios: Its entry trigger mills the top three physical library cards into its controller's graveyard, or all remaining cards if fewer than three remain.

Pay three generic, black and green mana and sacrifice this creature as activation costs; return one targeted creature or Spacecraft card from its controller's graveyard to the battlefield on resolution.
Accept a Spacecraft card even when it is not a creature; reject a card of neither type and a card in another player's graveyard.
Enforce sorcery timing: its controller's main phase, priority and empty stack. The newly sacrificed Broodtender cannot be chosen as its own target because targets are chosen before costs.
If the target leaves the graveyard before resolution, return nothing; the paid mana and sacrificed Broodtender are not refunded.

requirements.name: Terramorphic Expanse
scenarios: Activating requires an untapped physical Expanse, taps and sacrifices it as costs, and puts its non-mana search ability on the stack.
Resolution may find one physical basic land card in its controller's library, puts it onto the battlefield tapped and shuffles the remaining library; the fetched copy cannot remain available to draw.
Reject a nonbasic land even if it has a basic land subtype; allow finding no card and still shuffle.

The fetched land is put onto the battlefield rather than played, so it does not consume another land play; neither the sacrificed Expanse nor the tapped fetched land supplies immediate mana by itself.

requirements.name: Mulldrifter
scenarios: Casting for four generic and one blue mana creates the 2/2 flying creature and its draw-two entry trigger, with no evoke sacrifice trigger.
Casting for the evoke cost of two generic and one blue mana still creates the entry draw trigger plus the evoke sacrifice trigger; its controller chooses their stack order.
The two triggers resolve independently: sacrificing Mulldrifter does not remove an already stacked draw trigger, and removing the creature does not refund its cast cost.
Reject payment that covers neither the selected normal nor evoke cost; do not treat evoke as simply reducing the cost without the sacrifice consequence.
Flying prevents blocking by a creature with neither flying nor reach; legal flying/reach blocks remain available.

requirements.name: Skeleton Crew
scenarios: Its continuous bonus gives each other controlled Skeleton or Pirate +1/+1, gives only one bonus to a creature with both types, and gives no bonus to itself or an opponent's creature.

While it is on the battlefield, one or more creature cards leaving its controller's graveyard in one event creates one 2/2 black Skeleton Pirate token; separate departure events produce separate triggers.
The generated token receives the Crew's bonus while both remain on the battlefield; removing the Crew removes that bonus without changing the token's base characteristics.
Paying five generic and one black mana from its graveyard returns this physical card to the battlefield tapped; that return does not trigger its own token ability.
Noncreature cards leaving the graveyard, or creature departures while this card is only in the graveyard, do not generate its token trigger.

requirements.name: Myriad Landscape
scenarios: It enters tapped; after untapping, its first activated ability taps it to add one colorless mana.
The search ability requires two generic mana, tapping and sacrificing this land; the same tap cannot also supply its colorless mana ability.
Find two physical basic lands sharing a land subtype, put both onto the battlefield tapped and shuffle; two Forests qualify but a Forest and Island do not.
Allow finding zero or one basic land and still shuffle; reject a nonbasic land and never duplicate one library card to satisfy two selections.
The fetched lands enter without consuming land plays, and the sacrificed Landscape stays in the graveyard even if the search ability is countered.

requirements.name: Exotic Orchard
scenarios: In a four-seat pod, one activation chooses one color that a land any current opponent controls could produce; a tapped opponent Forest still permits green.
An opponent's colorless-only land does not permit colorless output, because colorless is not a color; with no qualifying colors an activation produces no mana.
If the only lands at all seats are Exotic Orchards, their circular references must not manufacture a color. Adding one Forest allows green to propagate through opposing Orchards.
Use the referenced lands' mana-ability effects and applicable replacements rather than whether their activation costs can currently be paid; do not actually tap or activate an opponent's land.
Changes of control or an opponent's elimination change the available opposing-land set for subsequent activations; do not cache an unconditional five-color output.

requirements.name: Glacierwood Siege
scenarios: Choose exactly Temur or Sultai as this enchantment enters; retain the choice for that object and enable only the corresponding ability.
With Temur chosen, casting an instant or sorcery triggers target-player mill four, including a legal self-target; countering the original spell does not undo that trigger.
Temur does not trigger from casting a creature, activating an ability, or merely copying a spell on the stack without casting it.

With Sultai chosen, allow land plays from its controller's graveyard while enforcing ordinary turn, priority, empty-stack and remaining-land-play restrictions; the permission neither grants an extra land play nor graveyard activated abilities.
A new entry requires a new choice; losing the enchantment removes the Sultai permission and must not leave a permanent player-wide flag.

requirements.name: Plaguecrafter
scenarios: In a four-seat pod, each player independently chooses one controlled creature or planeswalker in active-player/nonactive-player order, with prior choices visible, then all chosen permanents are sacrificed simultaneously.
The controller may choose Plaguecrafter itself; a player with both a creature and a planeswalker chooses which to sacrifice, rather than Plaguecrafter's controller choosing for them.
Only players unable to sacrifice a qualifying permanent choose a card to discard; make those choices in turn order without revealing the cards, then discard them simultaneously.
A player with a qualifying permanent cannot elect to discard instead; a player with neither a qualifying permanent nor a card in hand does nothing.
The effect does not target players or permanents and affects its controller as well as opponents; resolve resulting death/discard triggers after the current ability finishes.

requirements.name: Eternal Witness
scenarios: On entry, choose a target card of any card type from its controller's graveyard; resolve the optional return to that player's hand or decline.
Reject a card in an opponent's graveyard, and do not offer the Witness on the battlefield as a graveyard target.
If the targeted physical card leaves the graveyard before resolution, return nothing and do not select a substitute; removing Witness itself does not cancel its existing trigger.

requirements.name: Llanowar Wastes
scenarios: Its colorless ability taps this land and adds one colorless mana without dealing damage.
Its other ability taps this land, adds one chosen black or green mana and deals one damage to its controller; reject blue, red, white and simultaneous black-plus-green output.
Damage is part of the ability's effect, not a life-payment activation cost; use the damage event machinery, including applicable prevention/replacement effects.
Do not prohibit activation solely because that damage would reduce the controller to zero life; apply state-based actions at the proper checkpoint. Either ability leaves the same land tapped.

requirements.name: Negate
scenarios: After legal payment of one generic and one blue mana, target and counter a noncreature spell on the stack, preventing that spell's effects and moving its card to the appropriate graveyard.
Reject a creature spell, including an artifact creature spell, as the target; also reject an activated/triggered ability or a permanent already on the battlefield.
If the target spell leaves the stack before resolution, do not counter a different spell; apply cannot-be-countered restrictions rather than assuming every legal target is countered.

requirements.name: Doombot Harbinger
scenarios: Its entry trigger offers the complete optional mill-four event: accept and mill up to the top four remaining cards, or decline and mill none.
When it dies, offer exiling this card from the graveyard; only performing that exile creates the separate reflexive return trigger.
Choose the target creature card in its controller's graveyard when the reflexive trigger goes on the stack, then return it to hand on resolution; the exiled Harbinger is no longer a candidate.
Declining exile, or the Harbinger leaving its graveyard before that choice resolves, yields no return trigger; removing the chosen target before its later resolution yields no return.
Its 2/1 body has flying: reject blocks by creatures lacking flying or reach while permitting otherwise legal flying/reach blocks.

requirements.name: Aftermath Analyst
scenarios: Its entry trigger mills three physical cards from the top of its controller's library, stopping at an empty library rather than inventing cards.
Pay three generic and one green mana and sacrifice this creature as activation costs; on resolution return every land card currently in its controller's graveyard to the battlefield tapped.
Return multiple lands simultaneously, including nonbasics, without consuming land plays; leave nonland cards and other players' graveyards unchanged.
The ability has neither targets nor a sorcery-only restriction: permit it whenever its controller may legally activate it, including with no lands to return.
Lands added to the graveyard before resolution are included, lands removed before resolution are not, and countering the ability does not refund its costs.

requirements.name: Baleful Strix
scenarios: Entering creates one mandatory draw-one trigger even when it entered without being cast; removing the Strix does not remove that stacked trigger.
As a 1/1 flying creature it cannot be blocked by a creature with neither flying nor reach; otherwise legal flying/reach blocks remain available.
Positive damage it deals with deathtouch makes a damaged creature subject to destruction at the proper state-based-action check; zero or wholly prevented damage does not.
Keep both artifact and creature types, so effects selecting either type can affect this same physical object without creating two objects.

requirements.name: Gray Merchant of Asphodel
scenarios: In a four-player pod with only this Merchant contributing black devotion, resolution makes each of the three opponents lose two life and its controller gain six life.
Determine black devotion from black mana symbols in currently controlled permanents' mana costs at resolution; count Merchant's two symbols only if it remains a controlled permanent.
Removing black-symbol permanents before resolution lowers X; black color alone or black symbols in rules text do not add devotion, and opponents' permanents do not count.
The effect is life loss rather than damage and gains only life actually lost this way; do not apply damage prevention to it or include the controller among the opponents.
Complete all instructed loss and gain before applying resulting state-based actions; do not cap an opponent's life loss at their pre-effect positive life total.

requirements.name: Dredger's Insight
scenarios: Its entry trigger mills four physical library cards, then optionally moves one artifact, creature or land card from those milled cards to its controller's hand.
Reject an eligible-looking card already in the graveyard before this mill and reject a milled instant or sorcery with none of the permitted types; allow declining the move.
One event moving one or more artifact and/or creature cards out of its controller's graveyard creates one gain-one-life trigger; an artifact creature is not counted twice.
Separate qualifying departure events create separate triggers, while a land-only departure or an opponent's graveyard departure does not trigger it.
Choosing a milled artifact or creature for its own entry ability causes its graveyard-departure trigger; choosing an ordinary land does not. Process that trigger after the entry ability finishes.

requirements.name: Elvish Mystic
scenarios: After paying green to cast it, a newly controlled Mystic without haste cannot activate its tap ability that turn because it is a creature.
Once continuously controlled since the start of its controller's most recent turn, an untapped Mystic may tap to add exactly one green mana.
Reject other colors, a second activation while tapped, or treating the same tap as both mana activation and attacking; a legally granted haste effect removes the new-control restriction.

requirements.name: Yavimaya Coast
scenarios: Its colorless ability taps this land and adds one colorless mana without dealing damage.
Its colored ability taps it, adds one chosen green or blue mana and deals one damage to its controller; reject black, red, white and simultaneous green-plus-blue output.
The damage is an effect, not paying one life: applicable damage prevention/replacement effects act on it, and insufficient life is not an activation-cost rejection.
At one life the activation can still occur, with any resulting loss handled at the proper state-based-action checkpoint; either choice taps the same land and prevents a second tap activation.

requirements.name: Undead Butler
scenarios: Its mandatory entry trigger mills the top three physical library cards, or all remaining cards when fewer than three remain.
Its death trigger offers exiling this card from the graveyard; accepting and performing that action creates a separate reflexive trigger targeting a creature card in its controller's graveyard.
Target choice occurs after the Butler is exiled, and resolving that trigger returns the targeted card to hand; the exiled Butler cannot return itself through that trigger.
Declining to exile or finding the Butler already absent from the graveyard creates no reflexive trigger; if the later target leaves, return nothing.
Exiling the Butler instead of its going from the battlefield to the graveyard is not dying and does not create the death trigger.

requirements.name: Transplant Theorist
scenarios: Its own entry and each other controlled artifact's entry trigger the optional draw-then-discard ability; an opponent's artifact or an ordinary nonartifact creature does not.
If multiple controlled artifacts enter simultaneously, create one trigger for each qualifying entrant rather than batching them into one trigger.
For each resolution, declining to draw also skips the discard; accepting draws one then requires discarding one with no action window between them.
Pay two generic mana to put a target card of any type from its controller's graveyard on the bottom of its library; do not shuffle or put the card on top.
The activated ability has no tap, sacrifice or sorcery-only restriction; reject an opponent's graveyard card, and return nothing if its target leaves before resolution.

requirements.name: Aether Spellbomb
scenarios: Pay one blue mana and sacrifice this artifact to target a creature; on resolution return that creature to its owner's hand, which may differ from its controller's hand.
Alternatively pay one generic mana and sacrifice this artifact to draw one card without targeting a creature.
These are separate abilities: one sacrificed physical Spellbomb cannot pay both costs, and neither ability requires tapping or waiting through creature summoning restrictions.
Reject a noncreature target for the bounce ability; if the chosen creature leaves before resolution, do not retarget and do not refund the sacrificed Spellbomb.

requirements.name: Fleshbag Marauder
scenarios: In a four-player pod, each player chooses one creature they control, including Marauder for its controller if desired; a player with no creature sacrifices nothing.
Collect choices in APNAP order and perform the sacrifices simultaneously; the ability does not target, and one player cannot choose another player's creature.
A creature entering after the trigger is on the stack is eligible at resolution; sacrifice-generated dies triggers wait until the complete ability resolves.

requirements.name: Swamp
scenarios: A legal untapped Swamp produces exactly one black mana and becomes tapped; it cannot also produce colorless or be tapped twice without untapping.
Playing it consumes the available land play, whereas putting it onto the battlefield with a search effect does not; a fetched Swamp obeys that effect's tapped instruction.

requirements.name: Izoni, Thousand-Eyed
scenarios: Count creature cards in the controller's graveyard when the enters trigger resolves, then create that many distinct 1/1 black-and-green Insect tokens; zero creates none and artifact creatures count once each.
Pay both black and green mana and sacrifice a distinct other controlled creature as costs to gain one life and draw one card; reject sacrificing Izoni itself or an opponent's creature.
Removing Izoni after activation does not undo the paid sacrifice or stop the ability; generated tokens retain exact colors/types and cannot become reusable graveyard cards.

requirements.name: Pernicious Deed
scenarios: Choose and pay X, sacrifice Deed as an activation cost, then simultaneously destroy every artifact, creature and enchantment with mana value at most X, across all players.
At X=0, affected zero-mana-value tokens are destroyed; ordinary lands and planeswalkers remain unless they also have an affected type. A multitype permanent is destroyed once.
The sacrificed Deed is already absent during resolution; an indestructible affected permanent survives, and the ability remains on the stack if its source leaves.

requirements.name: Trading Post
scenarios: First mode requires one mana, an untapped Post and a real discarded hand card; pay once and gain four life. An empty hand cannot satisfy its cost.

Second mode requires one mana, tap and one life; create exactly one 0/1 white Goat. At zero life the payment is illegal; paying the last life is legal but subsequent state-based loss is not deferred until resolution.

Third mode chooses an artifact-card target already in your graveyard before paying the creature sacrifice; return it only if still legal. A creature artifact sacrificed to pay cannot become a newly chosen target afterward.

Fourth mode pays one mana, taps Post and sacrifices a controlled artifact, which may be Post itself, then draws one card. Paying any mode taps the same physical Post and does not finance another tap activation.

requirements.name: Skullclamp
scenarios: Equip for one mana targets a creature you control and obeys sorcery timing; reject an opponent's creature or a target that becomes illegal before resolution.
An equipped 1/1 becomes 2/0 and dies at the next state-based check; its death triggers two card draws while the Equipment stays on the battlefield unattached.

Moving Skullclamp between creatures removes the old +1/-1 and adds it to the new creature; simultaneous destruction of Equipment and equipped creature still uses the pre-event attachment for the dies trigger.

requirements.name: Llanowar Elves
scenarios: After continuous control since the start of the turn, tapping Llanowar Elves produces exactly one green mana; summoning sickness and an already tapped state each prevent that activation.
Casting it costs green mana before it is on the battlefield; the creature cannot pay for its own spell or be counted as immediate untapped acceleration without a haste permission.

requirements.name: Sol Ring
scenarios: Pay one generic mana to cast Sol Ring; once resolved as an untapped noncreature artifact it may tap immediately for exactly two colorless mana.

Paying a one-generic cost from that output leaves one colorless mana in the pool until the applicable step/phase boundary; its output cannot satisfy a colored symbol and one tap cannot be spent twice.

requirements.name: Nyx Weaver
scenarios: Reach permits blocking a flying attacker but does not grant flying; the upkeep trigger mills two only at its controller's upkeep and handles a library with fewer cards.
Pay one generic, black and green and exile Weaver from the battlefield as costs to return a target card already in your graveyard; Weaver cannot target itself after paying the exile cost.
Its enchantment and creature types both remain available to Muldrotha's type-choice permission; choosing one must not consume both permissions.

requirements.name: Shriekmaw
scenarios: The enters trigger requires a creature that is neither an artifact nor black; reject either excluded property, and if no legal target exists do not invent a target or retarget later.
Casting for evoke one generic plus black creates the same creature spell and produces both its enters-removal trigger and evoke-sacrifice trigger; the controller may order these triggers.

Casting for its normal cost does not create an evoke-sacrifice trigger; countering the spell produces no enters effect. Fear permits blocks by artifact creatures or black creatures and rejects other blockers.

requirements.name: Crop Sigil
scenarios: At your upkeep, permit either milling exactly one available top card or declining; this does not trigger at another player's upkeep.

Activation requires at least four distinct card types among cards already in your graveyard before costs; supertypes and creature subtypes do not count, and sacrificing Sigil cannot make an otherwise illegal activation legal.

Choose zero or one creature-card target and independently zero or one land-card target in your graveyard; reject an extra target in either group, pay two generic plus green and sacrifice Sigil, then return only still-legal targets.

requirements.name: Beast Within
scenarios: A legal permanent of any type can be targeted; on resolution destroy it and have its controller create one 3/3 green Beast, preserving the distinction between controller and owner.
An indestructible legal target survives but its controller still creates the Beast; if the sole target is illegal before resolution, neither destruction nor token creation occurs.

requirements.name: Ravenous Chupacabra
scenarios: Entering creates a removal trigger targeting a creature currently controlled by an opponent; choose among all living opponents' creatures rather than one hard-coded seat.
A target changing to your control before resolution is illegal; an indestructible still-legal creature is not destroyed. With no legal creature target, do not generate a phantom removal action.

requirements.name: Witherbloom Command
scenarios: Choose exactly two distinct modes on casting, with legal target domains for those modes; resolve chosen modes in printed order rather than policy-selected order.

First mode targets a player to mill three, then chooses a land non-targetingly from your entire graveyard, including a just-milled land if you were the target; it never returns a land from another player's graveyard.

Second mode accepts only a noncreature, nonland permanent of mana value at most two; third applies -3/-1 to a target creature until end of turn; fourth targets an opponent for two life lost and gives you two life.
If every chosen target is illegal, the spell does not resolve; if at least one remains legal, perform the applicable instructions without supplying new targets for illegal ones.

requirements.name: Liliana, Death's Majesty
scenarios: Use the frozen starting loyalty; permit a loyalty activation only with the required loyalty and normal once-per-turn sorcery timing. Pay the loyalty change when activating, not at resolution.
+1 creates a distinct 2/2 black Zombie token, then mills two; the token and mill both occur even if no library cards remain, without treating milling as drawing.

-3 targets a creature card in your graveyard and returns it under your control, adding black and Zombie while retaining its other colors and types; this effect follows that battlefield object, not a later zone-changed object.

-7 simultaneously destroys all non-Zombie creatures across the pod, including yours; Zombies and indestructible creatures survive for their respective reasons, and multitype Zombies are not accidentally excluded.

requirements.name: Stitcher's Supplier
scenarios: An enter event and a later battlefield-to-graveyard dies event each create their own mill-three trigger; removing the source after either event does not cancel the pending trigger.
Exiling Supplier instead of its dying does not create the dies trigger; milling it directly from library to graveyard also does not count as dying.

requirements.name: Tasigur, the Golden Fang
scenarios: Delve may exile zero through five chosen cards from your graveyard to pay the generic portion of the unmodified printed cost; it cannot pay the black symbol or exile an unavailable card twice.

Actual mana spent, not printed mana value or exiled-card count, contributes to expend; exiling multiple creature cards as one delve payment must preserve grouped versus each-card graveyard-leaving events.
The activated ability pays two generic plus two independently chosen green/blue hybrid symbols, mills two, then lets a chosen opponent select a nonland card from your entire resulting graveyard.
The returned card and the opponent are resolution choices rather than spell targets; the controller cannot substitute its preferred card, a land cannot be chosen, and no nonland card means no return.

requirements.name: Underground River
scenarios: Choose between tapping for colorless without damage and tapping for exactly one blue or black mana with one damage to the controller; one physical tap produces only the chosen output.

The damage is an effect, not a life-payment requirement: a player at one life may activate the colored ability, with resulting damage and state-based loss processed correctly. Do not silently waive or turn it into a pay-life cost.

requirements.name: Kairi, the Swirling Sky
scenarios: Flying restricts legal blockers; an opponent-controlled spell or ability targeting Kairi triggers ward three, whereas its controller's targeting does not. On ward resolution the responsible opponent chooses to pay or have that spell/ability countered.

Choose exactly one dies-trigger mode. First mode allows zero or any number of distinct nonland permanent targets whose combined mana value is at most six; a total of seven is illegal even if every individual target is small.
Return still-legal first-mode targets to their owners' hands, not their controllers' hands; ward and ordinary target legality continue to apply to each selected target.
Second mode mills six, then chooses zero through two instant and/or sorcery cards non-targetingly from the entire resulting graveyard; newly milled cards qualify and permanent-only cards do not.

requirements.name: Foundation Breaker
scenarios: The enters trigger targets an artifact or enchantment and allows declining destruction at resolution; an optional effect does not permit an invalid target or a creature lacking both required types.

Evoke one generic plus green creates an enters-sacrifice trigger in addition to the optional removal trigger; normal casting does not. Order simultaneous own triggers legally and preserve each trigger if the source is sacrificed first.

requirements.name: Grim Reaper's Scythe
scenarios: A single event moving one or more creature cards out of your graveyard creates exactly one 2/2 black Zombie; noncreature-only movement and another player's graveyard movement create none. Separate events can each trigger.

At sorcery timing pay three generic plus black, tap Scythe and sacrifice two distinct controlled creatures, then return the previously chosen legal creature-card target from your graveyard with a finality counter.
The two sacrificed creatures cannot be newly chosen as the existing activation's target; a later-illegal target is not replaced and the paid costs remain paid.

A finality counter replaces that permanent's battlefield-to-graveyard move with exile, preventing dies triggers; losing abilities does not remove this counter effect, multiple finality counters are redundant, and returning to hand is unaffected.

requirements.name: Fellwar Stone
scenarios: Tapping produces exactly one chosen color that some opponent-controlled land could produce under the applicable rules; a colorless-only opponent land does not provide a color.

Compute candidates from current opponents and land abilities, not their commander identities or a cached all-colors assumption; an opponent land being tapped is not itself grounds to remove its possible colors.
With no qualifying color, activation cannot fabricate mana. Sharing a source definition with Exotic Orchard must preserve distinct physical taps and the artifact's casting cost.

requirements.name: Spore Frog
scenarios: Sacrificing Frog is the activation cost and requires controlling it, but requires neither mana nor tapping; a newly cast Frog may activate despite summoning sickness.

After resolution, prevent all combat damage that would be dealt during the rest of this turn to any recipient across the pod, including players, creatures and planeswalkers; do not prevent noncombat damage or carry prevention into the next turn.
Destroying/removing the Frog after activation cannot undo the paid sacrifice or prevention ability; damage already dealt before resolution is not reversed.

requirements.name: Molt Tender
scenarios: The tap-to-mill ability puts one top library card into your graveyard and produces no mana; distinguish it from the separate tap-plus-exile mana ability.

For mana, exile one chosen card already in your graveyard as a cost and tap to add exactly one mana of a chosen color. No graveyard card, summoning sickness or an already tapped Tender prevents that activation.
The same tap cannot both mill a card and exile that newly milled card for mana; paying exile emits the correct graveyard-leaving event and cannot be rolled back after the ability resolves.

requirements.name: Living Death
scenarios: Perform three ordered stages: all players exile their graveyard creature cards; all players sacrifice their controlled creatures; each player returns its own previously linked exiled cards to the battlefield.
Track exact physical cards exiled by the first stage. Creatures sacrificed in the second stage, or exiled by a finality replacement then, are not added to the return set.
Each stage preserves simultaneous multi-card events; distinguish one-or-more triggers from per-card triggers and defer placing all triggered abilities on the stack until resolution completes.

Nobody receives priority between stages; noncreature graveyard cards remain, tokens sacrificed do not become returnable cards, and a linked card that is no longer in the expected exile zone cannot be fabricated back. Command-zone state-based choices do not occur between its exile and return stages; a commander returned by this effect is already back on the battlefield at the post-resolution checkpoint.

requirements.name: Evolving Wilds
scenarios: Tap and sacrifice Wilds, then search your own library for one basic land, put it onto the battlefield tapped and shuffle the remaining library; this is not a land play.
A legal search may find no basic even if one exists; a found card must satisfy the basic-land predicate, be removed from its exact library position and never remain available for a later draw.

requirements.name: Kheru Goldkeeper
scenarios: Flying applies in combat; while Goldkeeper is on the battlefield, a single event moving one or more cards out of your graveyard during your turn creates one Treasure, regardless of those cards' types.

Separate events may each trigger, but movement on an opponent's turn or from another player's graveyard does not. The trigger does not function from Goldkeeper's own graveyard merely because renew is activated there.

Renew is available only from your graveyard at sorcery timing: pay two generic, black, green and blue and exile this exact card, then put two +1/+1 counters and one flying counter on the chosen legal creature.

Treasure is a distinct artifact token with tap-and-sacrifice for one mana of any color; it cannot be spent twice. Flying counters remain separate from +1/+1 counters and do not add repeated flying abilities for extra counters.

requirements.name: Island
scenarios: An untapped Island produces exactly one blue mana when tapped; it cannot satisfy a black or green symbol solely because the commander has those colors.
Normal play consumes a land play; a search effect that puts it onto the battlefield tapped consumes the library copy without spending an additional land play.

requirements.name: Forest
scenarios: An untapped Forest produces exactly one green mana when tapped; surplus green may pay generic but not a required blue or black symbol.
Normal play and search-based placement use the same physical-card ledger but only normal play consumes a land play; a tapped fetched Forest cannot produce mana immediately.

requirements.name: Unseal the Necropolis
scenarios: Each living player mills three available top cards; afterward the caster chooses zero through two creature cards from its entire resulting graveyard and returns them to hand.
The returned cards are not preselected targets and may have just been milled; reject a third card, a noncreature card or a card in another player's graveyard.

requirements.name: Eccentric Farmer
scenarios: Its enters trigger mills three first, then allows returning one land card from the controller's entire resulting graveyard, including one milled in this resolution.
The land choice is optional and non-targeting; choosing none is legal, but choosing a nonland or an opponent's land is not, and library shortfall does not suppress the later choice.

requirements.name: Circle of the Land Druid
scenarios: On entering, choose either to mill four available top cards or decline; do not implement this as choosing an arbitrary number from one through four.

A later dies trigger chooses a land-card target in your graveyard when put on the stack and returns it only if legal at resolution; exile is not dying and a newly available land cannot replace an illegal target.

requirements.name: Mind Stone
scenarios: After paying two generic to cast the noncreature artifact, an untapped Mind Stone can immediately tap for exactly one colorless mana.
Its draw ability requires one generic, tapping and sacrificing this exact artifact. It cannot first tap itself for mana and then use that same tap to pay for drawing without an intervening untap.

requirements.name: Executioner's Capsule
scenarios: Pay one generic plus black, tap and sacrifice Capsule to target a nonblack creature; a creature that is black in addition to another color is excluded.

Choose the target before paying costs and recheck it at resolution; if it becomes black or leaves the battlefield, retain paid costs without destroying a replacement target. Indestructible is distinct from illegal.

requirements.name: Woodland Cemetery
scenarios: Check for a Swamp or Forest subtype among permanents you control as Cemetery enters: either subtype permits untapped entry, and a land merely producing black or green does not.
Without either subtype it enters tapped; later gaining or losing a qualifying land does not retroactively change that entry. Each legal tap adds exactly one chosen black or green mana.

requirements.name: Counterspell
scenarios: Pay two blue and target a spell currently on the stack; permanents on the battlefield and activated or triggered abilities are invalid target categories.

A successfully countered spell goes to its appropriate destination without resolving; an uncounterable spell remains on the stack, and a spell that leaves before Counterspell resolves cannot be replaced with a new target.

requirements.name: Ashiok, Sculptor of Fears
scenarios: Use the frozen starting loyalty and normal loyalty timing/payment restrictions; reject -5 or -11 without sufficient loyalty and a second activation of the same object during one turn.
+2 draws one card for the controller before every player mills two; distinguish drawing from milling and process an empty-library draw loss at the next state-based check, not as a successful draw.

-5 targets a creature card in any player's graveyard and returns it under your control while preserving its owner; it cannot target a battlefield creature or silently restrict choices to your graveyard.

-11 targets one opponent and changes control of all creatures that opponent controls at resolution; creatures they gain later are not included, the effect has no end-of-turn duration, and leaving-game cleanup respects ownership.

requirements.name: Grapple with the Past
scenarios: Mill three before choosing whether to return one creature or land card from your entire graveyard; a newly milled qualifying card is eligible and a card with both types still counts as one card.
The optional return is a resolution choice rather than a cast-time target; decline is legal, but returning two cards, a nonqualifying card or an opponent's card is not.

requirements.name: Trailtracker Scout
scenarios: Its tap ability adds one mana of a chosen color and observes creature summoning sickness; this mana activation itself does not count as mana spent casting a spell.

When this Scout is present as its controller spends the eighth total mana casting spells in a turn, create one expend trigger targeting zero or one permanent card in that controller's graveyard; reject instant/sorcery-only targets.

Count actual mana spent across spells, including additional casting costs, but exclude activated-ability payments, life payments and delve-exiled cards. Spending the ninth through sixteenth mana does not retrigger expend eight that turn.

Previously spent mana contributes to the turn total, but entering after the eighth mana was spent does not trigger retroactively; a new turn resets the count, including opponents' turns on which the controller casts instants.

requirements.name: Acolyte of Affliction
scenarios: Its enters trigger mills two before an optional non-target choice of one permanent card from your entire resulting graveyard; just-milled artifacts, enchantments, creatures, lands or planeswalkers can qualify.
Returning no card is legal; an instant or sorcery without a permanent type cannot be selected, and library shortfall does not cancel the remaining instructions.

requirements.name: Fyndhorn Elves
scenarios: Tapping a legally available Fyndhorn Elves adds exactly one green mana; the same physical creature cannot produce mana both before and after being counted as tapped without an untap.
A newly controlled creature without haste cannot use its tap ability even though a newly controlled noncreature Sol Ring can; paying the green casting cost precedes any battlefield mana production.

requirements.name: Overwhelming Stampede
scenarios: At resolution, compute X once from the greatest current derived power among creatures you control, then give the creatures in that affected set +X/+X and trample until end of turn.

Removing the largest creature before resolution can change X; removing it afterward does not shrink the existing bonus. A creature entering your battlefield afterward is not added to the affected set.
Expiration removes only this effect, retaining printed trample, counters and other power modifications; casting with no controlled creatures cannot invent an affected creature or a positive bonus.

requirements.name: Sakura-Tribe Elder
scenarios: Sacrifice Elder as the activation cost without tapping or mana; it can activate during its first turn on the battlefield despite summoning sickness.

Search your own library for one basic land, put a selected card onto the battlefield tapped and shuffle; allow a legal failure to find, and do not search the graveyard or treat this placement as a land play.
The sacrificed Elder is already in its new zone before resolution and cannot both remain a battlefield mana source and be available for graveyard recursion as the same current object.

requirements.name: Muldrotha, the Gravetide
scenarios: During the controller's own turn, permit one graveyard land play and one graveyard permanent spell for each permanent type, with normal timing, land-play limits and costs; do not grant instant/sorcery casting or opponent-turn permissions.

Choose which permanent type pays the permission for a multitype card such as Baleful Strix or Nyx Weaver when casting; consume only that type, and reject a second use of the same permission for that Muldrotha object and turn.

If Glacierwood Siege also grants a graveyard land play, choose and record the land permission used instead of consuming every available permission. For a permitted permanent spell, an allowed alternative cost such as evoke remains payable.

A new Muldrotha object entering in the same turn supplies fresh permissions, but does not create an extra land play. Removing Muldrotha after a permitted cast begins does not retroactively invalidate the cast.

In the fixed four-seat pod, each copy starts in its owner's command zone outside the seven-card hand; distinguish initial command casting, subsequent commander tax, ordinary graveyard casting and owner choices after zone changes.

requirements.name: Splinterfright
scenarios: Its characteristic-defining ability works in every zone: power and toughness each equal the creature-card count in its controller's graveyard if the object has a controller, otherwise its owner's graveyard; update after relevant zone events rather than freezing printed stars to zero.
An artifact creature card counts once and a creature token is not a creature card; entering with zero toughness is handled by state-based actions, including other simultaneous continuous modifiers.
Its upkeep trigger mills two during your upkeep and can change its derived size; trample uses the resulting combat characteristics and does not itself change the graveyard count.

requirements.name: Extract from Darkness
scenarios: Each player mills two, then the caster chooses a creature card from any graveyard and puts it onto the battlefield under its control; newly milled cards qualify and owner identity remains unchanged.
The choice is non-targeting at resolution, not limited to cards just milled or to your graveyard; if no creature card exists, do not create one or choose a noncreature.

requirements.name: Satyr Wayfinder
scenarios: Reveal the top four available library cards, optionally choose one land only from that revealed set for your hand, then put all remaining revealed cards into your graveyard.

An older graveyard land or unrevealed library card is not eligible; declining selection moves all revealed cards to the graveyard, and fewer than four library cards are handled without a shuffle or fabricated cards.
The selected land is revealed to opponents rather than hidden, while unexamined library order remains hidden; selecting it is not drawing it or playing a land.

requirements.name: Sivriss, Nightmare Speaker
scenarios: Pay the tap and sacrifice another controlled creature or a controlled artifact; summoning sickness prevents the tap cost. Sivriss cannot sacrifice itself merely as the creature, but could if it actually also qualifies as an artifact.

Resolve each opponent in turn order separately: mill one card, offer that opponent the choice to pay three life, and return that exact just-milled card from your graveyard unless payment was made; then proceed to the next opponent.

A player with less than three life cannot pay; legal exact-life payment and later state-based loss retain correct timing. Different opponents may make different decisions; never batch all milling before those choices.
If a milled card never reaches or no longer occupies the expected graveyard, do not return a different card. Separate successful returns cause separate graveyard-leaving events.
Choose a Background adds no runtime partner, Background card or command-zone permission while Sivriss is in this frozen deck's library; its construction relevance must not mutate the fixed pod.

requirements.name: Codex Shredder
scenarios: The first ability taps to target any legal player, including its controller, and mills exactly one available top card; it produces no mana and cannot be retargeted after activation.
The second ability pays five generic, taps and sacrifices Shredder to return a previously chosen card from your graveyard; Shredder cannot choose itself after paying the sacrifice cost.
Both abilities share one physical tapped state; an illegal return target preserves paid costs, while first-ability milling must not be reported as drawing.

requirements.name: Seal of Primordium
scenarios: Sacrifice Seal as the entire activation cost to target and destroy an artifact or enchantment; tapping and mana are not required, and activation is not restricted to sorcery timing.
A creature without either required type is not a legal target; if the chosen permanent becomes illegal before resolution the sacrifice remains paid and no replacement target is selected.

requirements.name: Along the Crooked Way
scenarios: Its enters trigger targets a creature card in your graveyard and returns that target only if still legal; the enchantment's presence may observe that return as a separate graveyard-leaving event.
Trigger once for each creature card leaving your graveyard, so a single event returning two creature cards creates two amass triggers; contrast with Grim Reaper's Scythe's one-or-more grouping.

For each amass Goblins one, choose a controlled Army and add one +1/+1 counter plus Goblin as an additional subtype; if none exists first create a 0/0 black Goblin Army. Do not create a separate token for every trigger when an Army already exists.

Pay one generic plus black to grant menace until end of turn to the Goblins and Orcs you control when the effect resolves; a creature with both types gains the ability once, and unrelated creatures or later entrants are excluded.
Menace requires at least two blockers when blocked; Army selection is a non-targeting choice and preserves any pre-existing Army creature types.

requirements.name: Opulent Palace
scenarios: Opulent Palace enters tapped unconditionally, including when returned or placed by an effect; it cannot produce mana before an untap permits tapping it.
Each tap produces exactly one chosen black, green or blue mana, never all three together; it is not a basic land and cannot satisfy a basic-land search predicate.

generated_objects.requirement: Create a 0/1 white Goat creature token.

generated_objects.name: Beast
generated_objects.requirement: The destroyed permanent's controller creates a 3/3 green Beast creature token, subject to the spell's full resolution rules.

generated_objects.name: Zombie

shared_requirements.requirement: Pin applicable Comprehensive Rules, Oracle snapshot and keyword/token definitions. These prose obligations are independent expected-result specifications; each requires executable assertions and cited evidence before its support row can close.

Engine owns all legal choices. Policies consume only their permitted observation and cannot infer hidden cards from omniscient state. Replaying a complete transcript and checkpoint preserves pending choices, continuous effects, RNG streams and canonical results.

Every nonempty Oracle paragraph has a span and card-specific scenario obligations; intrinsic basic-land abilities and all cost/keyword/characteristic fields remain required even if Oracle text is empty. Multiple clauses in one paragraph all need executable assertions; span presence alone never grants support.

The seven generated token families require full canonical definitions and shared engine primitives. Capture and validate all reachable generated behavior; unrelated related-card links do not expand the exact pod.

scenarios: Record the responsible choosing player, timing, exact legal domain and information visibility for every target, mode, optional action, payment, ordering, permission and resolution-time choice; reject a choice submitted for the wrong player or decision instance.

A policy may bound candidate generation, but the executor must validate any submitted choice against the full rule-defined domain. Never convert a policy cap into a rules prohibition or silently omit a legal branch.
Optional effects with required targets still select targets at the correct stack-entry time; up-to targets permit zero, while non-targeting resolution choices are not subject to target restrictions.

Trigger and replacement choices, including reflexive triggers, pause at their actual decision boundary. A When-you-do trigger gets its targets only after the enabling action happened; an If-you-do instruction remains part of its resolving effect.
Use four distinct players with 400 physical cards across four copies of the fixed 100-card manifest; an opponent means every currently opposing living player, not a hard-coded second seat.
Apply APNAP ordering to simultaneous triggers and prescribed simultaneous choices, while retaining explicit sequential instructions such as Sivriss. Reveal only information the rule makes public.

Check player loss and multiplayer object/control cleanup at legal state-based checkpoints, without interrupting a resolving effect between its instructions. An eliminated player's objects and controlled effects require ownership-aware handling.

Commander designation follows the designated physical card across zones; command-zone casting permission, commander tax, replacement/state-based owner choices and combat-damage totals do not become ordinary printed abilities.
Command-zone cast counts belong to the proper commander and player; casting the same card from a graveyard does not charge command-zone tax merely because it is a commander.

After control changes or zone changes, preserve owner identity and recompute legal permissions from the actual state. Four identical Oracle commanders must never share one physical identity or tax counter.
Each seat starts with its designated commander outside its shuffled 99-card library and draws seven from that library; the commander never occupies one of the seven initial hand slots.

Apply the explicitly configured multiplayer Commander mulligan and first-turn draw policy, and log keep/bottom decisions with correct information visibility. Mulligans reshuffle the same physical cards using the canonical RNG.

Replaying the recorded setup and decision sequence reproduces the dealt hand, bottom-card order and later draws; reaching a configured policy limit must not be reported as an optimal keep recommendation.
Resolve instructions in their printed order without intervening player priority; effects do as much as possible unless a rule, condition or all-targets-illegal check prevents resolution.

Distinguish damage, life loss and life payment; distinguish destruction, sacrifice, exile and countering. Damage prevention must not prevent life loss or convert an unaffordable cost into a legal activation.

Once a trigger or activated ability exists on the stack, ordinary removal of its source does not erase it. Use last-known information and linked object sets where the applicable operation requires them.
Emit the actual event graph, preserving simultaneous groups and separate actions; never derive all triggers from one flattened list of moved cards.
Maintain one location per physical object, preserve printed identity separately from zone-object identity and never duplicate a card when drawing, searching, returning or controlling it.
Distinguish reveal, mill, draw, search, among-those selection and ordered bottom placement; preserve unexamined hidden library order and shuffle only when instructed.
Library shortfall mills/reveals only available cards; attempting to draw an unavailable card has its own loss semantics. A search of a hidden zone for specified qualities may legally fail to find.

Countered effects or invalid later targets do not undo earlier paid costs. Leaving a zone invalidates old-object targets and ordinary temporary links except where rules explicitly track the moved object.

Separate base characteristics, characteristic-defining abilities, counters and continuous modifications; evaluate affected objects, controller, timestamps and dependency order without copying derived values back into printed definitions.
Continuous static effects update when the source, controller, type or relevant graveyard changes; effects that fix an affected set or X at resolution retain the specified snapshot.
Expire only the correct until-end-of-turn effects; retain unrelated counters and printed abilities. Finality is a counter-created replacement effect rather than an ability granted to the permanent.

Use one canonical payment and source ledger: choose one output alternative per activation, pay all activation costs, keep genuine excess mana and tapped state, and empty pools at the correct boundaries.
Land plays are restricted by turn and remaining land allowance; effect-based battlefield placement does not consume a land play. Determine entry conditions before the new object can activate.

Source colors are actual ability outcomes, not produced_mana metadata. Opponent-dependent could-produce relationships require condition/replacement-aware evaluation that does not manufacture colors from circular Orchard references.
A creature tap ability needs continuous control or an applicable haste exception; a newly resolved noncreature artifact does not have that creature restriction.

Targeted recursion fixes its targets before payment; untargeted mill-then-return selects from the specified post-mill domain during resolution. Among-the-milled and entire-graveyard domains are different.
Grouped one-or-more departure triggers fire once per qualifying event; per-card triggers fire for each qualifying card. Artifact creatures meet both type predicates but are one card.
Casting/play permissions are attached to the appropriate source object and turn, selected explicitly if multiple permissions apply, and remain separate from timing, cost and land-play limits.
Preserve exact linked exiled-card sets across multi-stage effects and finality replacements; cards sacrificed later are not retroactively part of an earlier exiled-this-way set.

Validate a complete legal cost choice before mutation, then pay mana, tap, sacrifice, discard, exile and life exactly once; unavailable resources or repeated physical objects reject the action without partial payment.
Alternative casting costs still cast a spell and must preserve their added consequences, such as evoke's sacrifice trigger; permission to cast does not waive required costs.

Generic, colored, colorless, X and hybrid requirements remain distinct; delve pays generic only. Mana actually spent casting feeds expend accounting, whereas non-mana payments and activated-ability payments do not.
Targets precede cost payment, so a sacrificed or exiled card cannot be selected afterward as the same activation's target; failure or countering after legal payment does not refund the cost.
Enforce flying/reach, fear, deathtouch, trample and menace on actual derived characteristics; target and blocker domains distinguish opponent players, creatures and planeswalkers as required.

Generated Insect, Goat, Zombie, Skeleton Pirate, Beast, Treasure and Goblin Army tokens have the exact corpus-required characteristics and distinct identities. Tokens leaving the battlefield do not become reusable cards.
Track attachments and equipment effects by the current object; state-based actions use the derived toughness and pre-event attachment information needed for death triggers.
Amass chooses an existing controlled Army or creates the defined Army only when none exists; add counters and the requested additional creature type without replacing existing subtypes.
Initialize loyalty from frozen characteristics; enforce sufficient loyalty, normal sorcery timing and one loyalty activation per permanent object per turn, paying the loyalty change as a cost.
A planeswalker reduced to zero loyalty leaves by state-based action, but an already activated ability remains pending as permitted; life totals and loyalty are not interchangeable.
Control-changing and reanimation effects retain card ownership and their specified duration/type/color changes, including correct cleanup when a player leaves the multiplayer game.

Exact rules revision, executable engine/policy/protocol digests and token definitions must be pinned before qualification.
